Tell your Realtor® and your lawyer before closing.

$700K Oakville home. What if rates rise 1%? Here is the monthly mortgage math.

Example only, computed with Canadian semi-annual compounding, 25-year amortization:
1) $700,000 home with 20% down ($140,000) = $560,000 mortgage.
2) $560,000 at 4.44% = about $3,081 a month.
3) $560,000 at 5.44% (1 point higher) = about $3,399 a month, about $318 more.
4.44% is the lowest 5-year fixed rate shown on Ratehub.ca on Nov 7, 2026; 5.44% is a hypothetical. Lenders also apply the stress test and debt ratios, so what you qualify for may differ.

Want help working out your own budget? Comment INFO to get full details, or call 905-452-4298.

Example only. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

frames.say: Oakville home, seven hundred thousand. Rates rise?
First, a seven hundred thousand dollar home with twenty percent down means a five hundred sixty thousand dollar mortgage.
Next, at four point four four percent over twenty-five years, your monthly mortgage is about three thousand eighty-one dollars.
Finally, at five point four four percent, it's about three thousand three hundred ninety-nine dollars a month.
So all in, a one percent rate rise adds about three hundred eighteen dollars to your monthly mortgage.

Milton condo buyer: you may move in before you own.

With interim occupancy: 1) You may move in before you legally own the unit. 2) You pay a monthly fee covering interest on the unpaid price, estimated taxes and common expenses. 3) Those fees are not credited toward your final purchase price. 4) Warranty coverage starts when interim occupancy starts, so register with Tarion promptly.

Source: Tarion, "What to expect if you have interim occupancy of your condominium unit." Ask your lawyer how your own agreement works.
